title: Optimize ground‑state geometry of SiN
action: Construct an initial linear SiN molecule (doublet, Si–N separation ~1.6 Å) and perform a DFT geometry optimization at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level using an open‑source quantum‑chemistry package. Save the final Cartesian coordinates (in Angstrom) as a standard XYZ file.
description: Optimized molecular geometry of the SiN cluster.
output_schema: Standard XYZ format: first line – number of atoms; second line – comment; following lines – element, x, y, z (in Å) for each atom. The file contains two atoms: Si and N.

title: Compute harmonic vibrational frequencies of SiN
action: Using the optimized SiN geometry, perform a harmonic frequency calculation at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level. Write all real harmonic frequencies (in cm⁻¹, one per line, in ascending order) to a plain‑text file.
description: Harmonic vibrational frequencies of the SiN cluster.
output_schema: One frequency (cm⁻¹) per line, sorted in ascending order. The diatomic molecule has exactly one vibrational mode.

title: Optimize ground‑state geometry of SiN₂
action: Construct an initial asymmetric linear Si–N–N molecule (triplet) with bond lengths ~1.8 Å (Si–N) and ~1.15 Å (N–N) and optimize at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level. Save the final atomic coordinates as a standard XYZ file.
description: Optimized geometry of the most stable isomer of SiN₂ (asymmetric linear SiNN, triplet).
output_schema: Standard XYZ format: first line – number of atoms (3); second line – comment; following lines – element, x, y, z (in Å). Atoms: Si, N, N (in the order Si–N–N).

title: Compute harmonic vibrational frequencies of SiN₂
action: Perform a harmonic frequency calculation on the optimized SiN₂ geometry at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level. Write all real frequencies (cm⁻¹, one per line, ascending) to a text file.
description: Harmonic vibrational frequencies of the SiN₂ cluster (three modes).
output_schema: One frequency (cm⁻¹) per line, in ascending order; exactly three lines.

title: Optimize ground‑state geometry of Si₂N
action: Construct an initial symmetric linear Si–N–Si molecule (doublet, Si–N ~1.64 Å) and optimize at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level. Save the final coordinates as a standard XYZ file.
description: Optimized geometry of the most stable isomer of Si₂N (symmetric linear SiNSi, doublet).
output_schema: Standard XYZ format: first line – number of atoms (3); second line – comment; following lines – element, x, y, z (in Å). Atoms: Si, N, Si.

title: Compute harmonic vibrational frequencies of Si₂N
action: Perform a harmonic frequency calculation on the optimized Si₂N geometry at the B3LYP/6‑311G(d) level. Write all real frequencies (cm⁻¹, one per line, ascending) to a text file.
description: Harmonic vibrational frequencies of the Si₂N cluster (three modes).
output_schema: One frequency (cm⁻¹) per line, in ascending order; exactly three lines.

title: Compile benchmark summary CSV
action: From the three optimized XYZ files, extract the equilibrium bond distances: Si–N for SiN; N–N and Si–N for SiN₂; Si–N for Si₂N. From the three frequency files, extract all harmonic frequencies. Compile a CSV file with the following columns: system (string), r_SiN (float, Å, null if not applicable), r_NN (float, Å, null if not applicable), freq1 (float, cm⁻¹), freq2 (float, cm⁻¹, null if not present), freq3 (float, cm⁻¹, null if not present). Frequencies must be listed in ascending order.
description: Aggregated benchmark results for SiN, SiN₂, and Si₂N with bond lengths and harmonic frequencies.
output_schema: CSV with header: system, r_SiN, r_NN, freq1, freq2, freq3. Each row corresponds to one system. r_SiN and r_NN are bond lengths in Å (null if not applicable). freq1, freq2, freq3 are harmonic frequencies in cm⁻¹ in ascending order (null if not present). The CSV must contain one row per system (SiN, SiN2, Si2N) with the corresponding computed values.
